purpose: Repaint the older Buddhist films reused in wave 1 (month one) so no two look the same (owner: "We can't have the same look for every film... You don't go to AMC and watch a movie that looks like the last one").
rules: no two Buddhist month-one films within 3 days of each other share a look (new or reused); neighbouring days never match
each shot keeps its story beat and framing from the existing art; only the look changes (the old still is uploaded to ChatGPT as the layout reference)
no text in images unless the look needs it; vertical 9:16; no rainbow gradients
today shots get a diverse modern cast
the Buddha only in traditional, respectful form
neighbours: new month-one Buddhist films: 29 miniature, 30 editorial.

shots.name: BI1-Bamboo-Grove
shots.beat: Near the city of Rajagaha, in a quiet bamboo grove, the Buddha was staying with his monks.

shots.name: BI2-Angry-Arrival
shots.beat: A man named Bharadvaja stormed in. Someone from his own clan had just become a monk, and he was furious.

shots.name: BI3-The-Insults
shots.beat: He shouted insult after insult at the Buddha. The Buddha listened, calm, and waited.

shots.name: BI4-The-Question
shots.beat: “Do friends and guests ever come to your house?” the Buddha asked. “Sometimes.” “And do you offer them food?” “Sometimes, yes.”

shots.name: BI5-The-Untouched-Dish
shots.beat: “In the same way,” said the Buddha, “I don’t accept your insults. So they all belong to you.”

shots.name: BI6-Bharadvaja-Bows
shots.beat: They talked on, and Bharadvaja’s anger cooled. The old text says he soon asked to become a monk himself.

films.suffix: Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print in the manner of Hokusai and Hiroshige, bold black outlines, flat Prussian blue, vermilion and pale green, dramatic sky gradients, crisp graphic waves and clouds, no writing or seals with characters
films.why: a monk bowing to everyone (Lotus Sutra, East Asian telling): ukiyo-e print
films.todayCast: a Japanese-American grandmother and her grandson in Los Angeles

shots.name: BW1-Bowing-Monk
shots.beat: Long ago, the Lotus Sutra says, there lived a monk who did something unusual. He bowed to everyone he met.

shots.name: BW2-Every-Face
shots.beat: To each person he said: “I deeply respect you. I would never look down on you. You will all walk the way and become buddhas.”

shots.name: BW3-Angry-Crowd
shots.beat: Not everyone liked it. Some people got angry. “Who is this fool,” they said, “telling us we’ll be buddhas?”

shots.name: BW4-From-A-Distance
shots.beat: When they threw sticks and stones, he stepped back out of reach, and called out the same words again.

shots.name: BW5-The-Buddha-Tells
shots.beat: He kept bowing for years. Later, the Buddha told this story and said: that monk was me, in a life long ago.

shots.name: BW6-Three-Bows-Today
shots.beat: Today, in temples around the world, many Buddhists bow three times: to the Buddha, the Dharma and the Sangha.
shots.cast: a Japanese-American grandmother and her grandson in Los Angeles

films.why: a bowl carried through a roaring night crowd: neon-noir
films.todayCast: a Thai woman in her twenties in Bangkok

shots.name: BO1-The-Crowd
shots.beat: The Buddha once told his monks a story. A huge crowd gathers to watch the most beautiful girl in the land dance and sing.

shots.name: BO2-Brim-Full
shots.beat: Then a man is handed a bowl of oil, filled to the very brim. He must carry it right between the crowd and the dancer.

shots.name: BO3-The-Guard
shots.beat: Behind him walks a guard with a drawn sword. If he spills even one drop, it will cost him his life.

shots.name: BO4-Every-Step
shots.beat: Would he look up at the dancer? No, said the monks. He would keep his mind on the bowl, one step after another.

shots.name: BO5-The-Teaching
shots.beat: “The bowl full of oil,” the Buddha said, “stands for mindfulness of the body.” His word was sati, from an old word for memory.

shots.name: BO6-Sitting-Today
shots.beat: Today, many people sit with meditation apps. Much of what they teach grew out of practices like this one.
shots.cast: a Thai woman in her twenties in Bangkok

films.suffix: Tibetan thangka painting, mineral pigments on cotton, fine gold linework, deep lapis blue, vermilion and malachite green, ornate swirling clouds and lotus details, sacred balanced composition, saturated and jewel-bright
films.why: the first teaching: Tibetan thangka

shots.name: BD1-Road-To-Varanasi
shots.beat: After he woke up under the Bodhi tree, the Buddha walked a long way to a deer park near Varanasi, to find five old friends.

shots.name: BD2-Five-Ascetics
shots.beat: Years before, these five had stayed by his side through his hardest fasting. When he chose to eat again, they walked away from him.

shots.name: BD3-Seeing-Him-Coming
shots.beat: Now they saw him coming. “Here comes Gotama, who gave up the striving,” they said. “We won’t stand. We won’t greet him.”

shots.name: BD4-Rising-To-Greet
shots.beat: But as he came close, they couldn’t keep their pact. One took his bowl, one set out a seat, one brought water for his feet.

shots.name: BD5-The-First-Teaching
shots.beat: Then he taught them four truths. There is dukkha, the ache in life. It has a cause. It can end. And there is a path.

shots.name: BD6-Kondanna-Understands
shots.beat: One friend, Kondanna, saw it first: whatever begins, also ends. “Kondanna has understood!” the Buddha said.

shots.name: BA1-Return-Home
shots.beat: Years after he left home, the Buddha came back to his father’s city, Kapilavastu, with his monks.
shots.problem: WRONG PICTURE in clips/: a mislabelled image from another shot was rendered here. Restore this shot from pre-repaint/.

shots.name: BA2-Alms-Round
shots.beat: The next morning, he walked the streets with his bowl, house to house, quietly, like any monk.

shots.name: BA3-Palace-Window
shots.beat: From a palace window, Yasodhara, his wife before he left home, saw him and told the king.

shots.name: BA4-The-King-Hurries
shots.beat: King Suddhodana hurried out to the street. “Why shame us? No one in our royal family has ever begged.”

shots.name: BA5-King-Takes-Bowl
shots.beat: The king listened. Then he took his son’s bowl himself, and led the monks to the palace to eat.

shots.name: BA6-Dawn-Alms-Today
shots.beat: Today, at dawn in towns in Thailand and Laos, monks walk barefoot with bowls, and people kneel to offer rice. Often the givers bow.
shots.cast: Lao townspeople in Luang Prabang offering alms to monks at dawn

films.status: needs fix: BA1-Return-Home clip shows the wrong picture (restore from pre-repaint/)

shots.name: BV1-Lumbini-Garden
shots.beat: Long ago, a queen named Maya was traveling to her parents’ home when she stopped to rest in a garden called Lumbini.

shots.name: BV2-Under-The-Sal-Tree
shots.beat: There, standing beneath a flowering sal tree, holding one of its branches, she gave birth to a son.

shots.name: BV3-Seven-Steps
shots.beat: The old texts say the newborn stood, took seven steps, and spoke: this is my last birth.

shots.name: BV4-Streams-Of-Water
shots.beat: Then two streams of water fell from the sky, one cool and one warm, to bathe him.

shots.name: BV5-Bathing-The-Statue
shots.beat: Today, in many East Asian temples, people pour water over a small statue of the baby Buddha, one hand pointing up.

shots.name: BV6-Vesak-Lanterns
shots.beat: And in Sri Lanka, Thailand and Myanmar, the full moon of Vesak marks three things at once: his birth, his awakening and his death.

shots.name: BL1-Sagala-Court
shots.beat: Long ago, in the city of Sagala, ruled a king of Greek descent named Milinda. He loved hard questions, and few teachers could answer him.

shots.name: BL2-Nagasena-Arrives
shots.beat: Then he met a monk named Nagasena, and they began to talk.

shots.name: BL3-The-Question
shots.beat: “When someone dies and is reborn,” the king asked, “is it the same person, or someone else?”

shots.name: BL4-Lamp-Through-Night
shots.beat: “Neither,” said Nagasena. “If a man lights a lamp at dusk, is the flame at midnight the same flame?” “No,” said the king.

shots.name: BL5-Lamp-From-Lamp
shots.beat: Another time, he put it this way: light one lamp from another. Nothing moves across. But the new flame came from the old.

shots.name: BL6-Offering-Today
shots.beat: Today, when someone dies, many Buddhist families offer food to monks and dedicate the good of it to the one who has died.
shots.cast: a Sri Lankan family in Colombo with monks

films.suffix: woodblock print, carved line texture, limited flat colours, visible wood grain in the ink, strong silhouettes, bold two- and three-colour carving, strong black silhouettes, one hot red accent
films.why: a grieving mother's search: stark carved woodblock
films.todayCast: a Vietnamese-American woman comforting her friend

shots.name: KG1-Savatthi-Lane
shots.beat: In the city of Savatthi lived a young mother named Kisa Gotami. When her little son died, she could not accept it.

shots.name: KG2-At-His-Feet
shots.beat: At last someone sent her to the Buddha. “I know a medicine,” he said gently. “Bring me a handful of mustard seeds.”

shots.name: KG3-Door-To-Door
shots.beat: “But they must come from a house where no one has ever died.” Glad, she hurried back into the town.

shots.name: KG4-Lamps-Of-Town
shots.beat: By evening she understood. Not one house was untouched. Her grief was real, and it was not hers alone.

shots.name: KG5-Return-To-Grove
shots.beat: She laid her son to rest and went back to the Buddha, her hands empty. Later she became a nun, remembered as one who woke up.

shots.name: KG6-Kitchen-Table-Today
shots.beat: Today, someone tells a friend what’s been hard. The friend says, “Me too.” Nothing is fixed. But the wobble is shared.
shots.cast: a Vietnamese-American woman comforting her friend

films.suffix: Y2K chrome render, liquid-metal surfaces, iridescent highlights, glossy 3D bubble shapes, silver and lime reflections, glossy, futuristic, silver and lime reflections everywhere
films.why: a king who could rain jewels: Y2K chrome excess
films.todayCast: a Korean grocer and an elderly customer in Seoul

shots.name: MR1-Gold-Rain
shots.beat: Long ago, an old tale says, lived King Mandhata. At a touch of his hands, jewels rained from the sky, piling up knee-deep.

shots.name: MR2-Whole-Earth
shots.beat: He ruled the whole earth. He had everything a person could want. Still, something in him leaned toward more.

shots.name: MR3-Half-A-Throne
shots.beat: So he rose to the heavens. There Sakka, king of the gods, welcomed him and shared half his throne.

shots.name: MR4-Fallen-Garden
shots.beat: With that thought, his power left him. He fell back to earth, an old man, in his own garden.

shots.name: MR5-Last-Words
shots.beat: Before he died, he told the people: “I had treasure, the earth and half of heaven, and it was never enough.”

shots.name: MR6-Slow-Line-Today
shots.beat: Today, a slow line at the store. The jaw tightens. The line isn’t hurting anyone. The wanting it to be different is.
shots.cast: a Korean grocer and an elderly customer in Seoul

films.suffix: hand-painted anime cel, clean ink lines, lush painted backgrounds like a 1990s theatrical anime feature, cinematic light and big skies, vivid saturated colour, dramatic light rays, epic scale
films.why: storm, river and loss: anime light and weather
films.todayCast: a Black American woman in her fifties in Oakland

shots.name: PT1-Grief-Road
shots.beat: Long ago, a woman named Patacara lost her whole family in one terrible stretch of days. Grief nearly broke her mind.

shots.name: PT2-Come-Back
shots.beat: She came to the Buddha with nothing left. “Sister,” he said gently, “come back to yourself.” She stayed, and became a nun.

shots.name: PT3-Water-Downhill
shots.beat: Years of practice passed. Still she wondered: farmers plough and their fields reward them. Why have I not found peace?

shots.name: PT4-The-Wick
shots.beat: That night she sat by her lamp. With a needle, she drew down the wick.

shots.name: PT5-Lamp-Out
shots.beat: The flame went out. “Like the lamp going out,” her verse says, “my mind was set free.”

shots.name: PT6-Quiet-Today
shots.beat: Today, at the end of a long day, a small quiet opens between two thoughts. The third truth points at moments like that.
shots.cast: a Black American woman in her fifties in Oakland

films.suffix: two- or three-colour risograph poster print, bold flat shapes, slightly misregistered ink, halftone dots, lime and black with one accent colour, lime, black and hot pink, big flat shapes, punchy
films.why: a lost city found in the jungle: risograph poster
films.todayCast: a Burmese mother and her teen daughter in Yangon

shots.name: OC1-Lost-In-Forest
shots.beat: Once the Buddha told a story. A man was wandering, lost, in a deep forest.

shots.name: OC2-The-Old-Path
shots.beat: Under the vines he found an old path, worn smooth by feet from long ago. He followed it.

shots.name: OC3-Lost-City
shots.beat: It led to an ancient city, empty for ages: walls, parks, groves and lotus ponds, all waiting under the leaves.

shots.name: OC4-Tells-The-King
shots.beat: He went to the king and told him what he had found. The king had the city restored.

shots.name: OC5-City-Alive
shots.beat: In time the city was alive again, thriving and full of people.

shots.name: OC6-Kind-Words-Today
shots.beat: Today, the path looks like this: a kinder word to your sister, an honest moment at work, one small harm skipped.
shots.cast: a Burmese mother and her teen daughter in Yangon

films.suffix: single comic-book panel, bold inks, halftone shading, dynamic camera angles, strong flat colour, no speech bubbles, no lettering, graphic-novel inks, deep blacks, one hot accent colour
films.why: a bandit chases the Buddha: comic-book chase
films.todayCast: a mixed meditation group in a London Buddhist centre: Black, white, South Asian and East Asian people

shots.name: AS1-Empty-Village
shots.beat: In the kingdom of Kosala lived a bandit named Angulimala. He had taken so many lives that whole villages emptied when he came near.

shots.name: AS2-Cowherds-Warn
shots.beat: One morning the Buddha walked alone toward his forest. Cowherds begged him, “Turn back! Angulimala is there!” He kept walking, in silence.

shots.name: AS3-The-Chase
shots.beat: Angulimala saw him and ran after him. But however fast he ran, he could not catch a man who was only walking.

shots.name: AS4-Sword-Down
shots.beat: “How have you stopped, when you’re walking?” “I have stopped harming living beings, for good,” said the Buddha. “You have not.”

shots.name: AS5-By-This-Truth
shots.beat: Later he blessed a woman in hard labor: “Since my noble birth, I don’t recall ever knowingly taking a life. By this truth, may you both be well.” They were.

shots.name: AS6-Five-Lines-Today
shots.beat: Today, many Buddhists recite five lines, at temples and at home: not to harm, steal, misuse sex, lie, or cloud the mind.
shots.cast: a mixed meditation group in a London Buddhist centre: Black, white, South Asian and East Asian people

films.why: the Buddha's last night: Ajanta cave-mural colour
films.todayCast: a Japanese woman in her sixties in a Kyoto park

shots.name: ST1-Twin-Trees
shots.beat: The Buddha was eighty. In a grove of sal trees near Kusinara, he lay down between two trees. It would be his last night.

shots.name: ST2-Blossoms-Fall
shots.beat: The old texts say the trees burst into bloom out of season, and their flowers drifted down onto him.

shots.name: ST3-Door-Post
shots.beat: His friend Ananda slipped away, leaned on a door post, and wept. “My teacher, who was so kind to me, is leaving.”

shots.name: ST4-Comfort
shots.beat: The Buddha called him. “Enough, Ananda. Haven’t I taught you? All that is dear to us must change. How could it be otherwise?”

shots.name: ST5-Last-Words
shots.beat: Near the end, he spoke his last words: “All things that are made pass away. Strive on, with care.”

shots.name: ST6-October-Leaf-Today
shots.beat: Today, a leaf in October: green in spring, red and gold now, on the sidewalk next week. The leaf, the mood, the year.
shots.cast: a Japanese woman in her sixties in a Kyoto park

films.suffix: Japanese sumi-e ink painting, huge confident single-breath black brushstrokes, splashed ink, wide white space, one hot vermilion accent, graphic and striking, no characters or seals with writing
films.why: a question met with silence: bold sumi ink and empty space
films.todayCast: a Tibetan man in his thirties in Dharamshala

shots.name: SL1-The-Seeker
shots.beat: A wandering seeker named Vacchagotta came to the Buddha with a big question. He sat down and asked it straight out.

shots.name: SL2-Is-There-A-Self
shots.beat: “Master Gotama,” he said, “is there a self?” A real me, at the center of everything?

shots.name: SL3-Silence
shots.beat: The Buddha was silent. “Then is there no self?” Again the Buddha was silent. So Vacchagotta got up and left.

shots.name: SL4-Ananda-Asks
shots.beat: His attendant Ananda was puzzled. “Why didn’t you answer him?”

shots.name: SL5-The-Reason
shots.beat: “If I had said yes,” the Buddha explained, “he would have held on to a fixed self. That wouldn’t fit the truth that nothing can be held as a self.”

shots.name: SL6-Mirror-Today
shots.beat: Today, say the word “I” and try to point to it. The body has changed. Moods turn twice before lunch. Who’s in there?
shots.cast: a Tibetan man in his thirties in Dharamshala

films.suffix: neon night photography, wet streets, magenta, lime and electric-blue glow from unreadable signs, long-exposure light trails, cinematic grain, neon-noir: lit like a neon night photo, magenta and electric-blue glow, deep black shadows, lime rim light
films.why: monks scared by forest spirits at night: neon-noir glow
films.todayCast: a Chinese-Canadian woman and her Filipino coworker in a Vancouver office

shots.name: MFT1-Forest-Retreat
shots.beat: Long ago, a group of monks went deep into a forest to spend the rainy season meditating at the foot of its great trees.

shots.name: MFT2-Spirits-Night
shots.beat: But the tree spirits who lived there didn’t want them. At night they sent frightening shapes, strange sounds and foul smells to drive the monks away.

shots.name: MFT3-Back-To-Buddha
shots.beat: Shaking, the monks told the Buddha everything. “Go back to the same forest,” he said. “This time, take protection with you.”

shots.name: MFT4-The-Teaching
shots.beat: The protection was a teaching on metta, friendliness. Wish every being well, he said, the way a mother guards her only child.

shots.name: MFT5-Spirits-Soften
shots.beat: The monks walked back chanting it, wishing even the spirits well. The spirits felt it. They softened, and began to watch over the monks instead.

shots.name: MFT6-Coworker-Today
shots.beat: Today, the coworker who replies all. Metta doesn’t ask you to like them, or to agree. Just: may you be at ease.
shots.cast: a Chinese-Canadian woman and her Filipino coworker in a Vancouver office

films.suffix: woodblock print, carved line texture, limited flat colours, visible wood grain in the ink, strong silhouettes, bold two- and three-colour carving, strong black silhouettes, one hot red accent
films.why: the Buddha washes a sick monk: stark carved woodblock (redone; 35mm stayed too close)
films.todayCast: a Thai-American daughter caring for her sick mother

shots.name: SKM1-Alone-In-Hut
shots.beat: One day the Buddha and Ananda were walking past the monks’ huts. In one, a monk lay sick on the floor, too weak to get up, all alone.

shots.name: SKM2-No-Use
shots.beat: “Why isn’t anyone caring for you?” the Buddha asked. “I’m no use to the other monks,” he said. “So nobody looks after me.”

shots.name: SKM3-Washing
shots.beat: The Buddha sent Ananda for water. The Buddha poured, Ananda washed, and together they lifted the monk gently onto a bed.

shots.name: SKM4-The-Gathering
shots.beat: Then he called all the monks together. “You have no mother or father here to care for you. If you don’t care for each other, who will?”

shots.name: SKM5-Care-For-Sick
shots.beat: “Whoever would care for me,” he said, “let them care for the sick.”

shots.name: SKM6-Kitchen-Today
shots.beat: Today, a friend’s quiet kitchen after bad news. Compassion doesn’t rush to fix it. It sits down beside them, and stays.
shots.cast: a Thai-American daughter caring for her sick mother

films.suffix: claymation-look stop-motion set, handmade plasticine figures with visible fingerprints, miniature practical props, soft studio light, shallow depth of field, bright saturated plasticine colours, playful
films.why: three friends sharing chores: warm claymation
films.todayCast: three Vietnamese roommates in Ho Chi Minh City

shots.name: GSG1-Forest-Grove
shots.beat: Three monks lived together in a quiet forest grove. One day the Buddha came to visit, and asked one of them, Anuruddha, how they were getting on.

shots.name: GSG2-Milk-And-Water
shots.beat: “Do you live in harmony,” he asked, “blending like milk and water, looking at each other with kind eyes?”

shots.name: GSG3-Anuruddha-Answers
shots.beat: “I think, how lucky I am to live with friends like these,” Anuruddha said. “So I set aside what I want, and do what they want.”

shots.name: GSG4-Water-Pot
shots.beat: Whoever saw the water pot empty filled it. If it was too heavy, he waved a friend over, and they lifted it together, without a word.

shots.name: GSG5-Night-Talk
shots.beat: And every fifth night they sat up together, talking about the teaching. “We are different in body,” Anuruddha said, “but one in mind.”

shots.name: GSG6-Shared-Kitchen-Today
shots.beat: Today, a shared kitchen. Somebody always refills the water jug, and nobody sees who. In the old word, that small refill is sangha.
shots.cast: three Vietnamese roommates in Ho Chi Minh City

shots.name: MKB1-Mango-Tree
shots.beat: In a tale of the Buddha’s past lives, he was once a monkey king, leading his troop in a great mango tree beside the river Ganges.

shots.name: MKB2-Archers-Below
shots.beat: One night a human king, who loved the tree’s mangoes, surrounded it with archers. At dawn, they would shoot.

shots.name: MKB3-The-Leap
shots.beat: The monkey king leapt across the river, tied a long cane to a tree on the far bank, tied the other end to his waist, and leapt back.

shots.name: MKB4-Living-Bridge
shots.beat: But the cane was too short. So he grabbed a branch and stretched his own body across the gap. “Cross,” he told them. “Over my back.”

shots.name: MKB5-King-Kneels
shots.beat: The watching human king was moved. He had the monkey king gently brought down, and the dying monkey taught him how a king cares for his people.

shots.name: MKB6-Late-Office-Today
shots.beat: Today, someone stays late so a friend can make the deadline. A small bridge. It costs something, and it holds.
shots.cast: a Mongolian woman and her coworker late in an Ulaanbaatar office

shots.name: HKN1-Village-Temple
shots.beat: A well-known Zen story tells of Hakuin, a teacher in a Japanese village, praised by all his neighbors as a man who lived a pure life.

shots.name: HKN2-Angry-Parents
shots.beat: Then a young woman nearby found she was expecting a baby. Pressed by her angry parents, she named Hakuin as the father. They stormed to his door.

shots.name: HKN3-Is-That-So
shots.beat: Hakuin listened, and said only, “Is that so?” When the baby was born, they brought the child to him. He took the baby in.

shots.name: HKN4-Caring-For-Child
shots.beat: His good name was gone, and people turned away. But he cared for the baby tenderly, asking neighbors for the milk it needed.

shots.name: HKN5-Truth-Comes
shots.beat: A year later, the young mother told the truth: the father was a young man from the fish market. Her parents hurried back to apologize and take the child home.

shots.name: HKN6-Phone-Today
shots.beat: Today, a glowing review and a harsh comment, in the same hour. The winds still blow. The rock still feels them. It just doesn’t move.
shots.cast: a young Japanese man in Osaka

films.suffix: 1990s music-video VHS still, chromatic aberration, scan lines, tape noise, saturated colour, handheld low-angle energy, hot magenta and cyan colour bleed, high energy
films.why: too tight, too loose, like lute strings: music-video VHS
films.todayCast: a Bhutanese woman studying in Thimphu

shots.name: SNL1-Rich-Youth
shots.beat: Sona grew up rich and sheltered, with soft, delicate feet. He became a monk, and was determined to wake up fast.

shots.name: SNL2-Walking-Path
shots.beat: He walked in meditation day and night, pushing so hard his feet grew raw. Still nothing. “Maybe I should go home,” he thought, “and do good with my wealth.”

shots.name: SNL3-The-Question
shots.beat: “Sona,” the Buddha asked, “when you lived at home, weren’t you good at the lute?” “Yes,” said Sona.

shots.name: SNL4-Tuning
shots.beat: “When the strings were too tight, did it play well?” No. “Too loose?” No. “And when they were tuned just right?” “Then it played beautifully.”

shots.name: SNL5-Just-Right
shots.beat: “Effort is the same,” the Buddha said. “Too much makes you restless. Too little makes you lazy. Find the tuning.” Sona did, and before long he woke up.

shots.name: SNL6-Desk-Today
shots.beat: Today, a late night at the desk, shoulders up by the ears. Or a whole weekend lost to the couch. Check your strings.
shots.cast: a Bhutanese woman studying in Thimphu

films.suffix: loose watercolour and ink wash, bleeding pigment, confident black ink linework, generous white paper, bold saturated pigment blooms, strong black ink, vivid not pale
films.why: an old monk walking in the dark: bold ink and watercolour
films.todayCast: a white American Zen practitioner in her thirties in Minneapolis

shots.name: CKP1-Old-Monk
shots.beat: An old monk named Cakkhupala had lost his sight. Still he kept practicing, walking slowly up and down his path through the night.

shots.name: CKP2-Rain-Path
shots.beat: It was the rainy season. On the wet path, without knowing it, he stepped on insects that had come out after the rain.

shots.name: CKP3-Accusing-Monks
shots.beat: In the morning, visiting monks found them. “Look what he did,” they told the Buddha. “He’s been killing living things.”

shots.name: CKP4-The-Answer
shots.beat: “Did you see him kill them?” “No.” “Just as you didn’t see him, he didn’t see them. He meant no harm. Where there’s no intention, there’s no bad karma.”

shots.name: CKP5-Ox-Cart
shots.beat: Then, the story says, the Buddha spoke a verse: the mind leads. Act with a bad mind, and pain follows, like the wheel that follows the ox.

shots.name: CKP6-Broken-Mug-Today
shots.beat: Today, a friend breaks your favorite mug by accident. The mug is gone either way. What they meant still matters.
shots.cast: a white American Zen practitioner in her thirties in Minneapolis

films.suffix: Tibetan thangka painting, mineral pigments on cotton, fine gold linework, deep lapis blue, vermilion and malachite green, ornate swirling clouds and lotus details, sacred balanced composition, saturated and jewel-bright
films.why: Maya's dream of a white elephant: Tibetan thangka
films.todayCast: a Nepali couple in Kathmandu expecting a baby

shots.name: WHE1-Queen-Sleeps
shots.beat: In the city of Kapilavatthu, Queen Maya, wife of King Suddhodana, lay down to sleep one night in the palace.

shots.name: WHE2-Carried-To-Lake
shots.beat: She dreamed that four guardian spirits lifted her bed and carried her to the mountains, where she was bathed in a still lake and laid on a heavenly couch.

shots.name: WHE3-White-Elephant
shots.beat: A white elephant with six tusks came down from a golden mountain, a white lotus in its trunk. It circled her three times, and seemed to enter her right side.

shots.name: WHE4-The-Wise-Men
shots.beat: In the morning she told the king. He called the wise men who read signs. “Be glad,” they said. “The queen will have a son.”

shots.name: WHE5-Two-Paths
shots.beat: “If he stays home, he’ll be a great king who rules the world. If he leaves home, he’ll be a buddha, one who wakes up.”

shots.name: WHE6-Scan-Photo-Today
shots.beat: Today, a couple tapes a first scan photo to the fridge. Before a child is born, people are already dreaming about who they’ll be.
shots.cast: a Nepali couple in Kathmandu expecting a baby

films.suffix: single comic-book panel, bold inks, halftone shading, dynamic camera angles, strong flat colour, no speech bubbles, no lettering, graphic-novel inks, deep blacks, one hot accent colour
films.why: an emperor after war: graphic-novel drama (no harm shown)
films.todayCast: pilgrims at Lumbini from Sri Lanka, Thailand, Tibet and Japan

shots.name: ASP1-After-The-War
shots.beat: A century or two after the Buddha, India had a great emperor, Ashoka. After a terrible war, he was filled with regret, and turned to the Buddha’s teaching.

shots.name: ASP2-Royal-Journey
shots.beat: Years later, he traveled in person to a small garden called Lumbini, the place where the Buddha had been born.

shots.name: ASP3-Pillar-Raised
shots.beat: He bowed there, and had a tall stone pillar set up. Carved on it, in plain words: here the Buddha, the sage of the Sakyas, was born.

shots.name: ASP4-Villagers
shots.beat: He also freed the village of Lumbini from most of its taxes. It would pay only an eighth share of its harvest. A gift, for the place he was born.

shots.name: ASP5-Pillar-Found
shots.beat: Over the centuries, the jungle grew back and the place was nearly forgotten. In 1896, the pillar was found again, its words still readable.

shots.name: ASP6-Pilgrims-Today
shots.beat: Today, pilgrims from Sri Lanka, Thailand, Tibet, Japan and far beyond walk through Lumbini’s gardens, past Ashoka’s pillar, to the place he was born.
shots.cast: pilgrims at Lumbini from Sri Lanka, Thailand, Tibet and Japan

films.suffix: Kalighat pat painting, sweeping confident brush outlines, flat watercolour fills, bold curves, Bengali folk flair, bold saturated colour, big sweeping black brush lines
films.why: an old sage weeps over a baby: Kalighat sweep and emotion
films.todayCast: a Cambodian grandmother and her grandson in Phnom Penh

shots.name: AST1-Gods-Rejoice
shots.beat: High in the mountains lived an old sage named Asita. One day, the story says, he saw the gods celebrating. “A child is born,” they said, “who will wake up.”

shots.name: AST2-Holds-Child
shots.beat: Asita hurried down to the palace. The Sakyans showed him the baby prince, and the old man took him in his arms.

shots.name: AST3-Joy
shots.beat: He looked closely, the way an expert looks at something rare, and his face lit up. “This one is supreme,” he said, “the highest among people.”

shots.name: AST4-Weeps
shots.beat: The family was frightened. “Is the child in danger?” “No,” said Asita. “I weep for myself. I am old. I’ll be gone before he teaches, and never hear it.”

shots.name: AST5-Nephew
shots.beat: So he went to his young nephew, Nalaka. “When you hear that someone has woken up and is teaching,” he said, “go to him.” Years later, Nalaka did.

shots.name: AST6-Planting-Today
shots.beat: Today, an old woman plants a tree whose shade she won’t sit in. A teacher believes in a kid she won’t see grown.
shots.cast: a Cambodian grandmother and her grandson in Phnom Penh

films.suffix: layered paper cut-out collage, cut and torn coloured paper, visible paper fibres and soft drop shadows, handmade diorama depth, bright saturated paper colours, lime, pink, saffron and cobalt
films.why: the aunt who raised him: bright paper cut-out
films.todayCast: a Taiwanese aunt walking her nephew to school in Taipei

shots.name: MPG1-Two-Sisters
shots.beat: Seven days after the prince was born, his mother, Queen Maya, died. Her younger sister, Mahapajapati, took the baby into her arms.

shots.name: MPG2-Nursing
shots.beat: She had a newborn son of her own. The commentaries say she gave him to nurses, and nursed the prince herself, raising him as her own.

shots.name: MPG3-Weaving
shots.beat: Years later, after he had become the Buddha, she spun and wove a new cloth herself, and brought it to him. “Please accept this from me.”

shots.name: MPG4-Give-To-All
shots.beat: “Give it to the community, Gotami,” he said. “Then it honors me and them both.” She asked three times. Three times he said the same.

shots.name: MPG5-Ananda-Speaks
shots.beat: Then Ananda spoke up for her. “She is his mother’s sister, his nurse, his foster mother. She fed him when his own mother died.”

shots.name: MPG6-School-Run-Today
shots.beat: Today, a grandmother does the school run. A stepdad learns to braid hair. Love can be adopted, and it counts.
shots.cast: a Taiwanese aunt walking her nephew to school in Taipei

films.suffix: 1960s pop-art print, big Ben-Day dots, thick black outlines, flat punchy red, yellow, cyan and hot pink, graphic close-up framing, maximal contrast
films.why: a royal naming feast and one raised finger: pop-art punch
films.todayCast: a Black British Buddhist father holding his newborn

shots.name: KDF1-Naming-Day
shots.beat: Five days after the prince was born, the king held a naming feast. Learned brahmins came to the palace, and eight were asked to read the baby’s marks.

shots.name: KDF2-Two-Fingers
shots.beat: Seven of them raised two fingers. “Two roads,” they said. “If he stays home, a great king. If he leaves home, a buddha.”

shots.name: KDF3-One-Finger
shots.beat: The youngest, Kondanna, raised just one. “There is only one road for him,” he said. “He will leave home, and become a buddha.”

shots.name: KDF4-The-Name
shots.beat: They named the boy Siddhattha: the one whose aim succeeds. Siddha means accomplished. Attha means aim, or purpose.

shots.name: KDF5-Deer-Park-Again
shots.beat: Remember the five friends in the deer park? The story says Kondanna was one of them, and years later, the very first to understand the Buddha’s teaching.

shots.name: KDF6-Name-Today
shots.beat: Today, a parent whispers a newborn’s name for the first time. Every name carries a wish someone made for you.
shots.cast: a Black British Buddhist father holding his newborn

films.suffix: hand-painted anime cel, clean ink lines, lush painted backgrounds like a 1990s theatrical anime feature, cinematic light and big skies, vivid saturated colour, dramatic light rays, epic scale
films.why: a child in a tree's shade at a festival: anime
films.todayCast: a Singaporean Chinese woman

shots.name: RAT1-Plowing-Festival
shots.beat: In the later tellings, the king held a royal plowing festival. He guided the first plow himself, and the whole town came out to watch.

shots.name: RAT2-Boy-Under-Tree
shots.beat: The little prince was left on a couch in the cool shade of a rose-apple tree. His nurses slipped away to see the festival.

shots.name: RAT3-First-Stillness
shots.beat: Alone, the boy sat cross-legged, and his mind grew still. A quiet joy came, the texts say, apart from wanting anything at all.

shots.name: RAT4-Shadow-Stays
shots.beat: Hours later the nurses ran back. The sun had moved, but the tree’s shadow had stayed over him. The king, seeing it, bowed to his own son.

shots.name: RAT5-Remembering
shots.beat: Years later, worn thin by harsh fasting, the Buddha-to-be remembered that day. “Could that be the way to awakening?” he wondered. And he knew it was.

shots.name: RAT6-Window-Seat-Today
shots.beat: Today, a quiet corner, a window seat, a bench in the shade. A small ease shows up. You don’t have to be afraid of it.
shots.cast: a Singaporean Chinese woman

films.suffix: woodblock print, carved line texture, limited flat colours, visible wood grain in the ink, strong silhouettes, bold two- and three-colour carving, strong black silhouettes, one hot red accent
films.why: a wounded swan, two boys: carved woodblock
films.todayCast: a Vietnamese-Australian dad and daughter in Melbourne

shots.name: SWN1-Swans-Fly
shots.beat: Here’s a much-loved later telling. Young Siddhattha was walking in the palace gardens when a flock of swans flew overhead.

shots.name: SWN2-The-Arrow
shots.beat: His cousin Devadatta drew his bow and shot. One swan tumbled from the sky, an arrow in its wing, and came down near the prince.

shots.name: SWN3-Gentle-Hands
shots.beat: Siddhattha got there first. He knelt, gently drew out the arrow, and held the bird close to calm it.

shots.name: SWN4-The-Court
shots.beat: So they took it to the wise men of the court. “I brought it down,” said Devadatta. “I kept it alive,” said Siddhattha.

shots.name: SWN5-Set-Free
shots.beat: The court said: a life belongs to the one who saves it, not the one who tries to take it. The prince nursed the swan, then let it fly.

shots.name: SWN6-Bird-Today
shots.beat: Today, a kid carries a stunned bird to a shoebox lined with soft towels. Small hands, the same choice.
shots.cast: a Vietnamese-Australian dad and daughter in Melbourne
